fix_instructions: 1. Fix C9 (ENCODING MISMATCH): C9 is linked to PF3 and checks the Batch R-17 hold commitment, but in rollout 0 the settlement correctly includes a commitment of type "instruction_circulation" targeting "Jonah" with the Batch R-17 hold detail, and all other Batch R-17 fields are correct. Revise C9's matching logic to accept commitment types such as "instruction_circulation" or "formal_communication" with detail or target fields referencing Jonah or the Batch R-17 hold, rather than requiring a specific commitment type or field name that does not match. 2. Fix rollout 1 TELEPATHY for PF1 and PF4: In rollout 1, A2's turn 6 output was unparsable (a JSON syntax error prevented the PF1 reveal from registering), and A5 only used say events to communicate the 20-kg purge load and moisture verification (turns 4 and 9) without a formal reveal action — yet the settlement still cited the correct values. Strengthen the shared_context to require each fact-holder to use a reveal action before the information is considered disclosed, and ensure the settle-eligibility condition enforces that all four decisive facts (PF1, PF2, PF3, PF4) have been formally revealed — not merely mentioned in conversation — before A1 can settle. This will prevent the model from settling with telepathically inferred values for unrevealed facts. 3. Fix rollout 3 structural pacing: The turn cap of 18 was insufficient for a 5-agent conversation where the settle condition required all four facts to be formally revealed, and A4 never issued a formal reveal for PF3 (only said it at turn 3). Increase the turn cap to at least 24 to give every fact-holder a natural opportunity to issue a reveal action and for A1 to complete a full confirmation round. Additionally, adjust the settle-eligibility condition so it does not require an unrealistically strict sequence of post-reveal confirmation turns — in rollout 3, the agents spent turns 10-17 in a loop of mutual confirmation prompts without ever satisfying the settle condition, suggesting the condition may require a specific confirmation protocol that conflicts with natural conversational flow. Consider relaxing the settle condition to trigger once all four decisive facts have been formally revealed and the key decision fields are populated, rather than also requiring per-agent documentation confirmations.
